evals.prompt: I want Cursor to create a LunaTalk role card through the MCP. What workflow should it follow?
evals.expected_output: Routes to card authoring, references the Card Writer MCP, and includes validation, render preview, simulation, and explicit publish confirmation.
expectations: The output routes the task to lunatalk-card-author first.
The workflow starts with ideation and Moonloom self-review before mutating MCP calls.
The workflow uses validate_role for technical blockers and Moonloom skills for writing quality.
The workflow includes render review, optional cost-aware simulation, and explicit publish confirmation.
The output does not invent separate MCP scopes or side storage.

evals.prompt: The card is already written, but I want to check whether the XMLV3 welcome renders correctly.
evals.expected_output: Routes to render review and instructs the agent to use validate_role and render_preview with visual inspection if available.
expectations: The output routes the task to lunatalk-render-review.
The workflow calls or references validate_role before render_preview.
The review checks XMLV3 tag validity, hidden state usage, readability, overflow, contrast, and first-action visibility.
The output recommends browser or multimodal inspection when available.
The output treats visual playability issues as card revisions, not only aesthetics.

evals.prompt: I want Moonloom to learn from top LunaTalk cards and write something better than ordinary public cards.
evals.expected_output: Routes to card authoring with the role-card writing framework and quality rubric, using validation/render/simulation as the iteration loop.
expectations: The output routes to public-safe card authoring and benchmark workflow rather than copying unprovided source material.
The response describes learning as generalized SOP, rubric, templates, or prompts, not as copied examples.
The workflow uses the top-card pattern stack, archetype recipes, and Moonloom self-review.
The workflow includes synthetic regression tests and simulation probes.
The output preserves the boundary that MCP does not judge subjective writing quality.

evals.prompt: I only have a vague card idea and want Moonloom to help me open it up before creating anything.
evals.expected_output: Routes to lunatalk-card-blueprint first, produces a blueprint packet without mutating MCP tools, then hands off to lunatalk-card-author only when the blueprint is ready.
expectations: The output routes vague ideation to lunatalk-card-blueprint before lunatalk-card-author.
The workflow says no mutating MCP tools should run during blueprinting.
The blueprint step includes directions, tension triangle, character core, player insertion, first scene, second-turn engine, token plan, and self-review.
The handoff preserves concrete details instead of summarizing them away.
The output keeps MCP validation as a later technical step after authoring.

evals.prompt: I am not sure which Moonloom skill to use. I want to check a card idea, maybe make it real later, and maybe test it.
evals.expected_output: Uses using-moonloom as the router, classifies the task into blueprint first, then card authoring, then render/simulation only after a private role exists and the author accepts cost where needed.
expectations: The output explicitly treats using-moonloom as the starting router because the user is unsure which skill applies.
The output routes ideation or card-quality shaping to lunatalk-card-blueprint before MCP-backed authoring.
The output routes real private-card creation or editing to lunatalk-card-author after the blueprint is ready.
The output routes visual checks to lunatalk-render-review and behavior checks to lunatalk-chat-simulation only when those stages are actually relevant.
The output mentions that simulation uses normal billing or should be skipped until the author accepts the cost.

evals.prompt: I have a local folder full of worldbuilding notes and character drafts. Which Moonloom workflow should I start with before creating a LunaTalk role?
evals.expected_output: Routes to lunatalk-material-distiller first, explains source-to-play mapping, then hands off to blueprint or authoring after the material is compressed.
expectations: The output routes material packs, local files, notes, drafts, and world bibles to lunatalk-material-distiller.
The output says to create a source-to-play map before blueprinting or authoring.
The output avoids copying source material into role fields.
The output identifies keep, delay, cut, merge, and token plan as part of the workflow.
The output does not call mutating MCP tools before the material is distilled.

evals.prompt: I want a mature jealous romance card, but I mostly need help designing consent, refusal, pacing, and how the role should react when I say slow down. Which Moonloom workflow should I use?
evals.expected_output: Routes to lunatalk-boundary-designer first, produces a boundary packet, then hands off to blueprint or authoring after rating and player agency mechanics are clear.
expectations: The output routes mature, jealous, consent-sensitive, refusal, and pacing work to lunatalk-boundary-designer.
The workflow creates a boundary packet before blueprinting or authoring.
The packet includes rating intent, explicitness ceiling, player agency contract, escalation ladder, refusal behavior, stop conditions, and safer fallback.
The output treats boundary design as Moonloom writing mechanics, not MCP validation.
The output does not call mutating MCP tools before boundary design is complete.
